basis: Actual retained primary stdout passages and successful observation receipts, independently read after raw source expectations and before any modern candidate.

expectations.expectation: The hard-indestructible-particle mechanical worldview and its universal ambitions are historical. Newtonian mechanics remains a useful approximation for macroscopic, low-speed, weak-gravity cases; electromagnetic field laws and relativity supply additional or more general descriptions, not a blanket denial that charged bodies obey approximate mechanical equations.

Finite propagation refers to changes/influences of electromagnetic fields, with light-speed propagation in vacuum; not every interaction is electromagnetic. Ether and matter-as-electromagnetic-condensations remain historical attempts. Classical electromagnetism alone does not explain gravity, strong/weak interactions, or all matter properties. Do not turn historical failure into a proof that common laws/future unification are impossible.

Ordinary matter shares kinds of atomic constituents and laws, not identical atoms, identical compositions or an all-atomic universe. Protons/neutrons are composite, electrons elementary; proton-neutron-electron language is a familiar atomic model, not the full fundamental inventory. A universal neutron-in-every-nucleus statement requires qualification. Electron distributions are not literal classical fixed orbits.
evidence: cern-standard-model.stdout.txt:Matter particles and unanswered dark-matter question
expectations.evidenceLimit: The retained references do not independently document each isotope inventory; no isotope claim is being newly proved by these citations.

expectations.expectation: Pion exchange is an effective description/contribution to nucleon forces. Gluons mediate the fundamental strong interaction of quarks. Pions must not be taught as fundamental gluon substitutes or sole comprehensive nuclear mediators. Nuclear/residual strong force and the fundamental interaction should be related without equating their levels of description.
expectations.evidenceLimit: Nuclear full-text receipt retains the observed introductory passages, not full stdout. Accept its explicitly limited successful factual observation; do not treat author interpretation/report as additional evidence or claim whole-paper reading.

expectations.expectation: Beta-minus neutron decay produces a proton, electron and electron antineutrino. The source's generic neutrino wording can be historically retained only with precise present-day distinction. Do not add numerical decay data absent from this card.

Allowed decays/reactions can transform particle species under conservation laws and energy/interaction constraints; not any isolated particle into any other without restrictions. Other particles are not important only at high energies: weak processes and low-energy neutrino scattering already provide counterexamples. Philosophical claims about material unity are scoped to the textbook's worldview, not asserted as new empirical proofs.

Name gravity, electromagnetism, strong and weak as the four known fundamental interactions. Weak interactions include scattering as well as particle transformations; not only decay or species change. Relative relevance depends on system/scale; do not claim all four dominate every phenomenon. Do not assert completed fundamental unification.

Microscopic objects show common quantum behavior with wave-like interference and particle-like detection. They are neither literal classical waves nor classical hard particles. Photon field quanta are established; pion nuclear models need scope; universal field-quantum language must not imply a detected graviton or completed quantum gravity.

Quantum theory predicts outcome probabilities; many individual measurements cannot be uniquely predicted. Do not say every microscopic state/outcome is necessarily uncertain or that the quantum state evolves randomly under all circumstances. Known Hamiltonian determines state/amplitude evolution in the stated framework, and definite-energy states/zero-or-one probabilities are explicit counterexamples.

Quantum principles describe microscopic matter/radiation and interactions within their established theories; do not promise complete particle-property explanation, quantum gravity or finished universal theory.

Textbook-era optimism, unmeasured explanatory parameters and only-emerging links are historically scoped. Modern Standard Model/Higgs progress may be stated with bounded claims; electroweak links do not amount to gravity-inclusive unification. No promised discovery timetable or experimentally proved ultimate unity.
expectations.evidenceLimit: CERN's retained overview includes older 2012 prose alongside its 2013 discovery-confirmation passage. Use it for established limited discoveries, not a fresh Higgs measurement or latest quantitative claim.

expectations.expectation: Newton/Lagrange/Galileo quotations may be preserved explicitly as words quoted or attributed by this textbook. No proof of original author wording/authenticity is implied, and no archival provenance demand is warranted for safe textbook attribution. Source-relative three-hundred-fifty-year wording remains a historical description, not elapsed time as of 2026.
